implementationFiles.role: Isaac control profile, H1 home pose, actuator configuration and collision-topology selection
Flat velocity task observations, commands, rewards, termination and AVBD extensions

adaptation.statement: AVBD independently reimplements selected Isaac Lab H1 flat-velocity configuration concepts and values in Swift on a separately sourced plant and AVBD physics. It is not an exact PhysX environment or policy port.

adaptedConcepts: implicit position-control stiffness and damping by joint family
300 Nm leg/torso/arm and 100 Nm ankle simulation effort limits
0.005 second simulation step and four-step control decimation
avbdDifferences: Menagerie MJCF supplies the plant instead of Isaac Lab USD
AVBD fixed-PD and contact solvers replace PhysX implicit actuators and contacts
AVBD uses its own solver iteration and stabilization settings
collision support sets are generated from separately attributed Menagerie meshes

adaptedConcepts: 69-value policy observation order and uniform corruption ranges
ten-second command resampling, two-percent standing commands, heading control and H1 velocity ranges
flat plane with no height scan or terrain curriculum
linear and yaw velocity tracking with 0.5 standard deviation
flat orientation, angular velocity, action rate, joint acceleration, ankle limit and nonessential-joint regularization
positive-biped air-time with flat-task threshold 0.6 and foot-slide penalty
torso-contact termination with a -200 per-second termination reward rate
avbdDifferences: reward rates are explicitly integrated over the 0.02 second AVBD control step
AVBD evaluation success criteria and metrics are not Isaac Lab reward terms
point-goal commands, physical projectiles and post-impact recovery are AVBD extensions
AVBD reset, contact measurement and batching implementations are independent

adaptedConcepts: Gaussian action standard deviation initialized to 1
clipped value and policy losses, gamma 0.99, GAE lambda 0.95, entropy 0.01, target KL 0.01 and gradient norm 1
avbdDifferences: MLX PPO is an independent implementation rather than RSL-RL
training run optimizer, minibatch, normalization, symmetry and schedule settings are checkpoint-specific
the manifest does not claim every AVBD H1 run uses the upstream recipe

markers: let rewardRate = trackingLinear[e] + trackingYaw[e] + feetAirTimeReward[e] - 0.25 * feetSlideCost[e] - orientationCost[e] - 0.05 * angularVelocityXYCost[e] - ankleLimitCost[e] - jointDeviationCost[e] - 0.005 * actionRate[e] - 1.25e-7 * jointAccelerationCost[e] - (fallen ? 200 : 0)

redistributionBoundary.statement: Only the BSD-3-Clause license and this attribution metadata are redistributed from the Isaac Lab provenance boundary; no upstream source, USD, mesh, texture or checkpoint payload is included.
